analysis.title: South Korea Tech: October 2026 export tracker: Another record-high DRAM exports at US$34bn (+595% yoy)
key_insights: South Korea October 2026 DRAM exports were US$33.8bn, +595% yoy, a record. Total memory exports were +359% yoy, the ninth consecutive month above +200% yoy and the second consecutive month above +300%.

NAND chip exports were +341% yoy and SSD exports +584% yoy in October. MOTIE attributes the strength to continued AI infrastructure investment by global big tech, which is sustaining memory price increases.
October 2026 had 22 working days against 20 in October 2025, which flatters yoy comparisons.
On a monthly basis, October memory exports fell 7% mom to US$50.1bn from US$54.1bn in September, and total semiconductor exports fell 6% mom to US$56.4bn. DRAM exports rose 2% mom.
GS expects 4Q26 Samsung Electronics memory revenue +358% yoy, with DRAM +348% and NAND +386% yoy.
GS expects 4Q26 SK Hynix total revenue +284% yoy, with DRAM +294% and NAND +260% yoy.

HBM proxy: YTD September Japanese epoxide resin imports to Icheon/North Chungcheong (SK Hynix, MR-MUF materials) are +8% yoy. YTD Japanese plastic film imports to Hwaseong/Pyeongtaek (Samsung Electronics, TC-NCF materials) are +53% yoy, which GS reads as implying potentially strong growth in Samsung HBM shipments.
In September alone, epoxide resin imports for SK Hynix were +35% yoy and plastic film imports for Samsung were +24% yoy.
Display exports were +29% yoy in October (OLED +31%, LCD +20%), reversing recent weakness. MOTIE attributes it to Korean manufacturers expanding regional electronics production.
GS expects 4Q26 LG Display revenue -7% yoy and Samsung Display +3% yoy.
MLCC exports were +37% yoy in October, the sixth consecutive month of double-digit growth. GS expects Samsung Electro-Mechanics MLCC revenue +71% yoy in 4Q26, led by AI server and auto MLCCs.
Li-ion battery exports were +21% yoy in October. Total battery exports were +38% yoy. MOTIE cites EV/ESS batteries, lead-acid batteries and battery parts.

Semiconductor wafer fab equipment (WFE) exports were +197% yoy and imports +77% yoy in October. GS attributes the import growth to memory makers' capex for technology upgrades and capacity expansion. WFE imports fell 35% mom after a September spike of US$2.8bn.
Total semiconductor exports were US$56.4bn in October, +259% yoy, against +263% in September.

market_movers.rationale: Samsung Electronics (005930.KS) common: Buy, 12m SOTP target W500,000 (EV/EBITDA, 2026E-2027E), set 8 Oct 2026. Last close cited W225,000. Memory revenue expected +358% yoy in 4Q26.
Samsung Electronics preference shares (005935.KS): Buy, target W380,000 using a 24% preferred-to-common discount. Last close cited W174,100.
SK Hynix (000660.KS): Buy, target W3,500,000 on 2026E/27E average P/E of 7.0x. Last close cited W1,418,000. 4Q26 revenue expected +284% yoy.

Samsung Electro-Mechanics (009150.KS): Buy, SOTP target W2,500,000 (2027E-2028E EV/EBITDA), set 28 Oct 2026, up from W2,400,000 on 9 Oct. Last close cited W1,196,000. MLCC revenue expected +71% yoy in 4Q26.
LG Display (034220.KS): Neutral, 12m forward P/B target W9,500 at 0.8x, set 22 Oct 2026, down from W10,000 on 15 Oct. Last close cited W7,320. 4Q26 revenue expected -7% yoy.

sector_views.rationale: Export data show DRAM +595% yoy and total memory +359% yoy, driven by AI infrastructure demand and rising memory prices. Buy on Samsung Electronics and SK Hynix.
MLCC exports +37% yoy with six months of double-digit growth. AI server and auto MLCC strength. Buy on Samsung Electro-Mechanics.
Exports rebounded +29% yoy in October, but 4Q26 revenue is expected -7% yoy at LG Display and +3% at Samsung Display. Neutral on LG Display.

earnings_insights: GS estimate (not yet reported) for Samsung Electronics 4Q26: memory revenue +358% yoy, DRAM +348% yoy, NAND +386% yoy.
GS estimate (not yet reported) for SK Hynix 4Q26: total revenue +284% yoy, DRAM +294% yoy, NAND +260% yoy.
GS estimate (not yet reported) for Samsung Electro-Mechanics 4Q26: MLCC revenue +71% yoy.
GS estimate (not yet reported) for LG Display 4Q26 revenue -7% yoy and Samsung Display 4Q26 revenue +3% yoy.

macro_indicators.interpretation: Record monthly DRAM exports, +2% mom, pointing to continued strength in memory pricing and AI-driven demand.
Ninth consecutive month above +200% yoy, down 7% mom from September.
Down 6% mom from the September high of US$60,295mn.
Back to positive growth after -5% in August and -10% in September.
Sixth consecutive month of double-digit yoy growth.
Strong growth in chipmaking equipment exports.
Consistent with memory makers' capex for technology upgrades and capacity expansion.

risk_factors: Samsung Electronics: major deterioration in memory supply/demand, sharp contraction in smartphone margins, mobile OLED market share loss.
SK Hynix: memory supply/demand deterioration and delayed technology migration, weaker smartphone/PC/server demand, Samsung HBM progress affecting HBM revenue and profit, lower AI-related capex.
Samsung Electro-Mechanics: stronger-than-expected industry MLCC supply increase, weaker AI server/auto/smartphone demand.
LG Display: higher or lower IT LCD panel pricing and TV OLED shipments.
October 2026 had two more working days than October 2025, inflating yoy comparisons.
charts_described: Exhibit 1 plots Hynix MR-MUF epoxide resin import value (US$mn, left axis) against Hynix HBM shipments (bn Gb, right axis) from 1Q23 to 3Q26, described as showing strong correlation.
Exhibit 2 plots SEC TC-NCF plastic film import value (US$mn, left axis) against SEC HBM shipments (bn Gb, right axis) from 1Q23 to 3Q26, described as showing strong correlation.
